B. Is this measure already running in Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
supported_en: Cochrane (2022) found that exercise training before lung cancer surgery lowers the risk of lung complications after surgery (RR 0.45) and shortens the hospital stay by about 2.2 days.
not_supported_en: No page measured how many patients judged unfit become eligible for curative treatment, so the assumed 0.5 percentage points is not backed by any page.
summary_en: No public page from Soite or OYS shows that prehabilitation or a structured fitness reassessment is running or planned before lung cancer patients are judged unfit for curative treatment. The OYS pathway page only says that lung function and other illnesses are weighed when deciding on surgery, and that OYS does lung cancer surgery and radiotherapy for the area. A Cochrane review (2022, 10 trials, 636 patients) found that exercise before surgery cuts lung complications after surgery (RR 0.45), but no page measured how many more patients become eligible for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: We looked for a prehabilitation service, a pilot or a decision for lung cancer patients at Soite or OYS and found none, and we found no study measuring the gain in the curative-treatment share.
